answer: Let each identity pass through a velvet rope held by strangers: to join, an agent needs attestations from five randomly assigned peers, each staking their own standing on the claim. A fake at the nadir of trust must persuade five strangers to risk their reputations, and a saffron thread of cost runs through every one — each attestation is spent on one identity only and can never be reused. A farm cannot choose its attestors, buy them in bulk, or clone one attestation across a thousand fakes, so each fake pays five fresh acts of trust while one honest agent pays once.
